items.title: Agentic AI Raises New Questions for Financial Institutions
items.summary:
DownloadDownload

Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved beyond answering questions and generating content. Increasingly, AI systems are being designed to act. Agentic AI can pursue objectives, make decisions and take actions on a user’s behalf, potentially with limited human involvement in individual decisions. [...] Consider a customer who gives an AI agent access to a bank account with an instruction to manage the customer’s cash efficiently. The agent decides to transfer funds, convert currencies or purchase an investment.

At first sight, these may appear to be ordinary customer transactions. Agentic AI, however, exposes important distinctions between identity, authentication, authority and attribution. [...] As agentic AI becomes more capable, firms may increasingly encounter interactions in which an AI agent collects information, compares products and initiates transactions for a customer. That creates a new layer between the institution and the person or entity with whom it has established a customer relationship.

Science, the report says, is being transformed by AI as it accelerates research timelines and opens up novel challenges. At the same time, the report cautions that "we will need to understand how AI-mediated information environments reshape collective cognition and moral behavior." The recent retraction of some 1,400 scholarly papers for failure to meet academic standards highlights the urgency of that message. [...] It identifies scaling as the engine of AI's advance, but also points to the growing cost and difficulty of obtaining training data as constraints on further progress.

The report likens AI's disruptive potential to that of the World Wide Web – without dwelling on the irony that the web itself is among the things being disrupted. It points to creative industries, computer programming, and mathematics as fields once deemed beyond the reach of automation that are now being upended. items.title: He’s using AI to screen existing compounds for therapeutic potential | University of Pittsburgh
items.summary: Developing pharmaceuticals using AI isn’t new, but it is laborious and often leads to a dead end. “If you generate a brand-new molecule, that’s actually a limitation,” Wang said. “A lot of compounds can’t be synthesized, and that is a big issue.” [...] This back and forth is the GAN’s training. Over time, the generator learns to generate fingerprints that more closely resemble those of real molecules. Researchers then search chemical databases for existing compounds with similar footprints; the AI-generated pattern leads to the discovery of real molecules that researchers can test — no need to synthesize a new molecule. [...] In a paper published Oct. 28 in the journal Science Advances, Wang outlined Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD), a novel, practical and reusable framework that takes advantage of generative AI to screen for existing compounds with potential for therapeutic development.

items.summary: Theo hướng dẫn, các giải pháp được xem xét công nhận là sáng kiến bao gồm: giải pháp kỹ thuật, giải pháp quản lý, giải pháp tác nghiệp và giải pháp ứng dụng tiến bộ kỹ thuật. Trong đó, giải pháp kỹ thuật có thể là sản phẩm, vật liệu, giống cy trồng, vật nuôi hoặc quy trình công nghệ; giải pháp quản lý là phương pháp tổ chức, điều hành công việc; giải pháp tác nghiệp là các phương pháp thực hiện nghiệp vụ chuyên môn; còn giải pháp ứng dụng tiến bộ kỹ thuật là việc áp dụng các giải pháp kỹ thuật [...] Đối với các đề tài khoa học, đề án khoa học và công trình khoa học – công nghệ, việc xét nghiệm thu thực hiện theo quy định của pháp luật về khoa học và công nghệ. Các đề tài chỉ được xem xét công nhận hiệu quả áp dụng và phạm vi ảnh hưởng khi đã được nghiệm thu đạt yêu cầu trở lên.

items.title: Focus sur un groupe de hackers étatique... CyberAv3ngers, l'unité cyber des Gardiens de la révolution que la France accu
items.summary:
Focus sur un groupe de hackers étatique... CyberAv3ngers, l'unité cyber des Gardiens de la révolution que la France accuse formellement d'avoir piraté nos frigos 🔎👇🏾

Depuis hier, tout le monde se pose la même question : c'est qui ces hackers iraniens qui ont fait dérailler les congélos d'environ 700 supermarchés français ?

Les faits 👉🏾

Pour rappel, le parquet de Paris vise Shahid Kaveh -une unité cyber offensive des Gardiens de la révolution iraniens-.
Selon les agences américaines, c'est le même groupe que CyberAv3ngers.

Sur Telegram, ils se présentent comme des hacktivistes pro-palestiniens -des militants qui piratent pour une cause-.
En réalité, pour Washington, c'est une unité d'État... un militaire qui opère en civil, en quelque sorte.

Et ils ont plein de faux noms : Storm-0784 chez Microsoft, Bauxite chez Dragos, Hydro Kitten, Cyber4vengers depuis janvier 2026, ...

Leur chef, Hamid Reza Lashgarian, est sanctionné par les États-Unis depuis 2024. Et Washington offre jusqu'à 10 millions de dollars pour des infos sur le groupe. Rien que ça...

Leurs faits d'armes 👉🏾

- Fin 2023 : au moins 75 automates du fabricant israélien Unitronics piratés aux États-Unis, en Israël, au Royaume-Uni et en Irlande. En Irlande, des habitants privés d'eau pendant plusieurs jours
- 2024 : un malware maison, IOCONTROL, pour piloter des objets connectés et des équipements industriels
- Octobre 2024 : selon OpenAI, ils utilisent ChatGPT pour repérer leurs cibles et corriger leur code
- Avril 2026 : en pleine guerre contre l'Iran, le FBI, la CISA -l'ANSSI américaine- et la NSA alertent sur leurs attaques contre l'eau, l'énergie et des mairies aux États-Unis
- Octobre 2026 : les frigos de nos supermarchés, avec une 20aine de départs de feu selon le parquet.

Pour rappel, un automate c'est lorsqu'un petit ordinateur pilote une machine : une pompe, une vanne... ou le dégivrage d'un congélo. Le thermostat de votre maison, mais pour une station d'eau... sauf qu'ils ne devraient pas être accessibles directement depuis Internet et encore moins avec des mots de passe par défaut 🤡

Là où ça devient totalement WTF 👉🏾

Leur méthode préférée ? Les mots de passe par défaut, sur des équipements branchés directement sur Internet...

En gros, des cambrioleurs qui ne crochètent rien... ils simplement trouvent la clé sous le paillasson.

L'unité cyber la plus redoutée des Gardiens de la révolution... qui entre avec des mots de passe d'usine. Parfois pirater c'est pas sorcier ! 
Merci à l'hygiène numérique déplorable de centaines de milliers d'entreprises et institutions ! 

Et le meilleur 👉🏾

Ils mentent beaucoup.

En 2023, ils revendiquent le piratage de la centrale électrique israélienne de Dorad, captures d'écran à l'appui... sauf que les images venaient d'une vieille fuite de 2022, recadrées et maquillées, selon DomainTools -une boîte d'analyse cyber-.

La moitié de leur arsenal, c'est de la propagande.
C'est aussi pour ça que l'attribution prend du temps : entre les vrais hackers, les faux hacktivistes et les revendications bidon -comme celle des groupes prorusses sur nos frigos-, il faut trier...

🙄

⚠️ Attention quand même

L'attribution française vise la vague d'octobre en France.
Les attaques contre des réseaux d'eau aux États-Unis cet été, au Minnesota notamment, restent des soupçons : aucune attribution officielle à ce stade.

Et pour rappel, la France n'est pas la première, les États-Unis inculpent des hackers iraniens depuis 2016, et l'Albanie a carrément rompu ses relations diplomatiques avec l'Iran après une cyberattaque en 2022 !

[...]

Cybèrement vôtre,

SaxX ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

results.input: Giải giúp mình bài toán tích phân: nguyên hàm của x^2 là gì?

result.actual_text:
Nguyên hàm của \( x^2 \) là một hàm mà khi lấy đạo hàm sẽ cho ra \( x^2 \). Nguyên hàm của \( x^n \) (với \( n \neq -1 \)) được tính theo công thức:

\[
\int x^n \, dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + C
\]

Trong trường hợp này, với \( n = 2 \):

\[
\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^{2+1}}{2+1} + C = \frac{x^3}{3} + C
\]

Vậy nguyên hàm của \( x^2 \) là \( \frac{x^3}{3} + C \), trong đó \( C \) là hằng số tích phân.

Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved beyond answering questions and generating content. Increasingly, AI systems are being designed to act. Agentic AI can pursue objectives, make decisions and take actions on a user’s behalf, potentially with limited human involvement in individual decisions. [...] Consider a customer who gives an AI agent access to a bank account with an instruction to manage the customer’s cash efficiently. The agent decides to transfer funds, convert currencies or purchase an investment.

At first sight, these may appear to be ordinary customer transactions. Agentic AI, however, exposes important distinctions between identity, authentication, authority and attribution. [...] As agentic AI becomes more capable, firms may increasingly encounter interactions in which an AI agent collects information, compares products and initiates transactions for a customer. That creates a new layer between the institution and the person or entity with whom it has established a customer relationship.

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: OpenAI’s Plan to Stop AI Data Centres Overloading the Grid | Energy Digital
items.summary:
A vocal section of the American electorate were seeking assurances that AI companies will not overload power grids, while many candidates ran on a ticket of holding hyperscalers to account.

Before a single vote was counted, though, OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT, had unveiled its ‘Grid Protectors Program’ – an initiative that will see its future computing campuses ease pressure on the grid. [...] “Data centres are paying more so families and small businesses can pay less, and our goal with every contract we sign under this framework is to deliver value for them,” she says

At OpenAI, the bigger picture is always in focus.

“With US data centre capacity projected to exceed 100 gigawatts by 2030⁠, we have a once-in-a-generation opportunity to strengthen the electric grid by building campuses that can adjust their power use when communities need it most,” the company says. [...] OpenAI is working to ensure its data centres can actually benefit grids, rather than overloading them. Credit: Anna Moneymaker/Getty

## What is OpenAI’s Grid Protectors Program?

The programme, which was announced on 2 November, commits the company to working with utilities, regulators and policymakers on arrangements for cutting the power use of its data centres at times of need.

items.title: Anthropic and OpenAI are coming for the development workflow | InfoWorld
items.summary: This is clearly where the frontier labs are moving, even though they’ve all benefited from an industry that provided neutral spaces to build. For example, OpenAI developed Pando, a Git back end for its own monorepo, to handle more engineers and agents reading and writing code concurrently. Its engineers kept using Git. OpenAI retained compatibility with the protocol and client and contributed improvements upstream. That compatibility let it rebuild the back end around the way its engineers [...] This pressure to maximize profitability helps explain why frontier labs like Anthropic and OpenAI are aggressively adding functionality to own more of the developer’s workflow. On November 4, OpenAI announced an agreement to buy Pierre, the company behind Code Storage and the open source libraries Codex already uses to browse files and review changes. OpenAI wants Codex to be where developers work, from the first branch an agent creates through deployment of the application. There’s money in [...] OpenAI or Anthropic could build the place developers prefer to work. The question is what happens when a team likes that place and wants a rival’s agent for a particular job. Maybe a startup has built a tool that can track down the intermittent test failure that’s had the team stumped for a week. Give it access to the code and test history the team has authorized, and it gets a chance to prove itself. Ask the team to move its work to a new platform first, and it probably never gets to try.

items.title: OpenAI wants to be Google - Fast Company
items.summary:
OpenAI needs to build analytics that show advertisers the consumer intent based on their prompts. I want to know which categories of intent my impressions ran against. I want to know whether those people were exploring, comparing, or ready to act, and which needs and product criteria drove that engagement. I want to know which kinds of sweater prompts turned into business and, just as important, which didn’t. Google’s advertisers have had some version of that map for two decades. It’s why [...] |

That comparison is where every sweater brand wants to be standing, and OpenAI has started selling the spot. Advertisers can buy on a CPM or CPC basis through OpenAI’s beta self-service Ads Manager, measure conversions with a pixel and Conversions API, and access campaign-level performance reporting. OpenAI is also testing Sponsored Agents, which let a user start a separate conversation with an advertiser after clicking an ad.

So the plumbing exists.

## A SEARCH-CALIBER AD PLATFORM [...] OpenAI already has the hard part down, the thing Google spent years teaching people to do. People are telling ChatGPT their goals, problems, preferences, objections, and purchase criteria in their own words. What it hasn’t built is the advertiser’s map of all that intent.

items.title: SpaceX, Anthropic and OpenAI: 3 giant IPOs and only 1 has sold shares
items.summary:
OpenAI has little reason to hurry while private investors keep funding it, and it has closed $11 billion in new money. The company has also given its own reason to wait. "We have not decided on timing yet; it may be a while because there are things we want to do that are likely easier as a private company," OpenAI said in a statement, as reportedby CNBC. Public buyers would also have to judge a trillion-dollar price without some basic facts about the business. Most of OpenAI's sales come from [...] The private valuation has climbed fast, and the figure public buyers will pay is still unsettled. Private investors valued OpenAI at $852 billion in late March, according to CNBC. Sam Altman, OpenAI's chief executive, is aiming for a $1 trillion valuation in the listing, according to Bloomberg reporting carried by The Next Web. That target is lower than what private investors last paid, which means the debut may not be priced at the private peak. Whether public buyers match the latest round or [...] The verdict on Anthropic will come only after trading begins, when buyers without a business stake decide whether $78 a share was worth paying.

## OpenAI

Illustration: Quartz

OpenAI has not yet sold a single share to the public, but private investors already value it at $1.25 trillion, according to Reuters. That valuation puts its planned listing among the largest stock market debuts. Nobody yet knows how much stock OpenAI will sell or when, so the size of its debut remains unknown.
